concerns.text: FR-002 requires the system to 'fail fast if GPU libraries are detected' and verify `torch.cuda.is_available()` returns False. The plan (Technical Context & Compute Feasibility) explicitly defines a 'GPU Escape Hatch' to auto-offload to Kaggle GPU if CPU constraints are exceeded. This creates a direct contradiction: the plan implements a fallback that violates the strict 'fail fast' requirement of FR-002. The plan must either remove the GPU fallback to satisfy FR-002 or the spec must be amended to allow GPU fallback under specific failure conditions.

FR-003 mandates generating '10-second video rollouts'. The plan (Compute Feasibility) states: 'Generating 10-second videos... may exceed the 6-hour limit... We will generate shorter rollouts (e.g., 2-3 seconds)... or reduce sample size'. The plan explicitly admits it may not fulfill the 10-second requirement, treating it as a variable to be reduced rather than a hard constraint. This leaves FR-003 unbacked by a guaranteed task in the plan.

FR-005 requires a Wilcoxon test on 'a minimum of 50 distinct trajectories'. The plan (Compute Feasibility) states: 'The plan will default to a fixed sample size (e.g., 10 trajectories) to ensure the job completes'. The plan explicitly plans to execute with N=10, which violates the N>=50 requirement of FR-005. There is no task in the plan to ensure 50 trajectories are processed; the plan anticipates failing this requirement.

SC-004 requires measuring 'computational efficiency (inference latency)' against the baseline. While the plan mentions 'Performance Goals' and 'CPU-First Strategy', it does not explicitly define a task or metric collection step for recording and comparing inference latency (time-to-completion) between the Baseline and DreamX-Lite variants. The plan focuses on MAE and statistical significance, but the specific task to measure and record latency for SC-004 is missing.
